description: We are Team Tonystark, building SPACE RELICS, an interactive archive of forgotten equipment on the Moon and Mars. We combine space research, software, data visualization and creative storytelling to bring these forgotten mission stories to life. We welcome members interested in space exploration, coding, AI/ML, design, research and storytelling.
summary:
SPACE RELICS is an interactive digital archive that brings the stories of human-made equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars to life. Developed as an educational exploration platform, it documents 13 artifacts across 11 space missions, explaining their original purpose, deployment, scientific contributions, operational history, and current known status.

Through an interactive artifact explorer, planetary map, mission timeline, scientific legacy section, and side-by-side comparisons, users can discover the stories behind forgotten space hardware. The project addresses the challenge by transforming scattered mission information into an engaging, accessible storytelling experience. It uses curated NASA and other scientific sources, with citations and transparent distinctions between verified, approximate, and uncertain information.

SPACE RELICS reminds us that even after missions end, their contributions to science and exploration remain.
details:
SPACE RELICS is an interactive digital archive that explores the human-made equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars. It allows users to discover individual artifacts, understand why they were sent, how they were used, what scientific contributions they made, and what is known about their present status.

The platform brings this information together through an Artifact Explorer, interactive planetary map, mission timeline, science legacy section, and side-by-side artifact comparisons. It covers 13 artifacts across 11 missions, turning scattered space-mission information into an accessible and engaging storytelling experience.

The project aims to make space exploration history easier to understand, encourage curiosity about planetary science, and highlight how equipment continues to contribute to scientific knowledge even after missions end. Its creative approach is to treat abandoned hardware not as discarded objects, but as historical artifacts with individual stories and scientific legacies.

We developed the project using JavaScript, React, Vite, Tailwind CSS, and Leaflet. The application uses curated local datasets and bundled NASA imagery, with cited sources and clear distinctions between verified, approximate, and uncertain information. We prioritised scientific accuracy, source transparency, usability, accessibility, and a responsive experience across devices. The result is a self-contained web application that can be explored without relying on live API connections.
